fact_check_verdict: PASS WITH MAJOR CORRECTIONS. Copper as cause is cut; keep only as Duffy's attributed Friday claim. CBS Nov 18: FAA and L3Harris concluded the Arkansas site where a NEW router was being deployed caused the outage, during a copper to fiber conversion. Mullin: new equipment was overwhelming the older system. Cause not final (Newsweek). SMART live status not verified either way. || PASS WITH CONDITIONS. SMART exists, ASI built it, about $875M over 12 years (covers FMDS and SMART), June 22nd. Limited ops September 21st DCA IAD BWI, all 22 en route centers November 10th. ASI denial verbatim (NBC, ABC, NPR). Mullin would not rule SMART out. Flyways numbers are company claims. No official ties SMART to the outage.

claims.spoken: On Friday November 13th the FAA halted departures at airports nationwide.
claims.verbatim_source: Paraphrase from fetch, not a quotation: AP reports the FAA halted most U.S. flights in a nationwide ground stop on Friday, November 13, 2026. Alaska Airlines says the FAA issued a nationwide ground stop on Friday, Nov. 13, affecting departures at origin for all airlines.

claims.spoken: Anchorage airport was part of the stop and every flight leaving the state was grounded.
claims.verbatim_source: "An official with Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport said flights traveling within Alaska are not impacted, but all flights going outside the state are grounded."
requires: attribute to an Anchorage airport official

claims.spoken: Flights within Alaska kept flying.
claims.verbatim_source: "Flights within the state of Alaska and Neighbor Island flights in Hawai’i are not impacted."
requires: say PER ALASKA AIRLINES and the Anchorage airport

claims.spoken: Alaska Air Group says it canceled nearly 600 flights, affecting more than 52,000 guests.
claims.verbatim_source: Paraphrase from fetch, not a quotation: In its Saturday Nov. 14, 10 a.m. PT update, Alaska Air Group said it had canceled nearly 600 flights since the ground stop began, affecting more than 52,000 guests.
requires: covers all of Alaska Air Group including Hawaiian, not only Alaska flights

claims.spoken: The stop lasted more than four hours.
claims.verbatim_source: "The FAA canceled the ground stop – which lasted more than four hours – around 5:30 p.m. Pacific on Friday, Nov. 13."

claims.spoken: It was only the second nationwide ground stop since September 11th 2001.
claims.verbatim_source: "This was only the second nationwide ground stop since September 11, 2001."

claims.spoken: On November 10th the FAA expanded SMART to all 22 of its en route air traffic control centers.
claims.verbatim_source: "all 22 of its Air Route Traffic Control Centers"

claims.spoken: That was three days before the nationwide ground stop.
claims.verbatim_source: Paraphrase from fetch, not a quotation: Latin Times says the expansion came on November 10, three days before the ground stop.
requires: the timing is a coincidence no official has linked to the outage

claims.spoken: SMART is an AI tool that reads weather, flight schedules and other data to predict congestion in the sky.
claims.verbatim_source: "analyzes weather, flight schedules and other operational data to predict congestion"

claims.spoken: SMART only makes recommendations. FAA staff decide whether to act, and it does not fly or control aircraft.
claims.verbatim_source: Paraphrase from fetch, not a quotation: AVweb says SMART gives scheduling recommendations to FAA personnel, who decide whether to act, and does not control aircraft or replace controllers.
requires: attribute the no-control point to the FAA

claims.spoken: A startup called Air Space Intelligence, or ASI, built SMART.
claims.verbatim_source: "ASI Selected by FAA to Modernize the National Airspace System"

claims.spoken: ASI said the ground stop was not caused by SMART.
claims.on_screen: "NOT BASED ON OR A RESULT OF THE SMART SYSTEM"
claims.verbatim_source: "The current ground stop is not based on or a result of the SMART system"

claims.spoken: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said SMART was completely disconnected from the equipment that failed.
claims.verbatim_source: "completely disconnected"

claims.spoken: On Friday Duffy blamed old technology, saying the FAA uses 1980s little copper lines.
claims.verbatim_source: "We use 1980s little copper lines."
requires: must be followed by the router findings g15 g16, never present copper as the cause

claims.spoken: The FAA and contractor L3Harris concluded the outage started at a site in Arkansas where a new router was being installed.
claims.on_screen: A NEW ROUTER · EL DORADO, ARKANSAS
claims.verbatim_source: "the Arkansas site, where a new router was being deployed, had caused the outage."
requires: say PER CBS NEWS citing the FAA and L3Harris
why it failed is not final, g19

claims.spoken: L3Harris was switching part of the FAA's network from copper wire to fiber when it failed.
claims.verbatim_source: "working on replacing a copper line with a fiber line"

claims.spoken: The FAA says devices flooded its telecom network, trying to connect 1,000 times every four to five seconds.
claims.verbatim_source: "attempting to connect 1,000 times every 4 to 5 seconds."

claims.spoken: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said new equipment being added was overwhelming the older system.
claims.verbatim_source: "it was overwhelming the older system."
requires: the thing overwhelming was the new equipment, per AP context

claims.spoken: Investigators have not made a final call on why the router failed.
claims.on_screen: WHY IT FAILED · NOT YET FINAL
claims.verbatim_source: "no final determination has been made about the exact cause of the failure."
requires: NBC, Duffy said officials must decide whether it was a faulty installation or a fault in the router itself

claims.spoken: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin would not fully rule SMART out.
claims.verbatim_source: "You can't rule out anything at this point."
requires: do not imply SMART is suspected

claims.spoken: Senate Commerce Democrats asked for an immediate pause on installing more of the new Juniper routers.
claims.on_screen: SENATORS ASK FOR A ROUTER PAUSE
claims.verbatim_source: "We request an immediate pause on the deployment of additional Juniper devices,"
requires: optional, same page, the upgrade converts 3,648 routers, per the contractor 400 installed and 69 operational

claims.spoken: In October more than two dozen lawmakers asked the FAA to pause SMART, citing a lack of transparency.
claims.on_screen: OCT · LAWMAKERS ASKED FOR A PAUSE
claims.verbatim_source: "egregious lack of transparency"

claims.spoken: Alaska Airlines has used ASI's Flyways tool since 2021.
claims.verbatim_source: "Alaska was the first airline to start using the Flyways system back in 2021"

claims.spoken: Flyways combines air traffic, weather and wind data and suggests more efficient routes to Alaska's dispatchers near Seattle.
claims.verbatim_source: "Additionally, the Flyways Dispatch application offers real-time insights and decision-making support to our dispatchers,"

claims.spoken: Alaska's operations chief says Flyways doesn't pick the route. The dispatcher does.
claims.verbatim_source: "It doesn't decide the route or waypoints that a dispatcher uses to get an airplane from A to B"
requires: attribute to Capt. Bret Peyton via NPR

claims.spoken: Alaska says Flyways saves roughly a million gallons of fuel and tens of thousands of flight hours a year.
claims.on_screen: ABOUT 1 MILLION GALLONS A YEAR · PER ALASKA
claims.verbatim_source: "Alaska says it's saving tens of thousands of hours in the air and roughly a million gallons of fuel per year"
requires: do not merge with 1.2 million 2023 figure

claims.spoken: Alaska Airlines describes Flyways as using advanced algorithms and machine learning.
claims.verbatim_source: "ASI's Flyways AI Platform utilizes advanced algorithms and machine learning to analyze vast amounts of data,"

claims.spoken: Air Space Intelligence, the company that makes the FAA's new AI tool SMART, said the ground stop was not caused by SMART.
claims.verbatim_source: Paraphrase from fetch, not a quotation: NPR reports the FAA recently began rolling out an AI-enhanced tool called SMART, and its maker, Air Space Intelligence, said the current ground stop is not based on or a result of the SMART system.
requires: a denial, not an independent finding

claims.spoken: SMART stands for Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories.
claims.verbatim_source: Paraphrase from fetch, not a quotation: AVweb and FLYING both expand SMART as Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories.

claims.spoken: An internal document shows the FAA is also trying to take an ownership stake in ASI.
claims.on_screen: FAA SEEKS A STAKE IN ASI
claims.verbatim_source: Paraphrase from fetch, not a quotation: Politico reports an internal FAA document showing the agency is working to acquire an equity stake or warrant in ASI.

claims.spoken: Per the contractor, the upgrade converts 3,648 routers, and 400 are installed with 69 operational.
claims.on_screen: 3,648 ROUTERS · 400 IN · 69 RUNNING · PER THE CONTRACTOR
claims.verbatim_source: Paraphrase from fetch, not a quotation: the Senate Commerce Democrats' release says the upgrade converts 3,648 routers and, per the contractor, 400 are installed and 69 are operational.
requires: say PER THE CONTRACTOR via Senate Commerce Democrats

cut: copper or legacy equipment as the established cause (contradicted by CBS: new router during copper to fiber conversion)
SMART caused or contributed (no official or outlet says so)
SMART not even plugged in (advocacy only)
five hours, longest in 25 years (AP only, conflicts)
ASI manages 40 percent of US traffic (vendor boast)

reserve.spoken: In June the FAA gave ASI a 12 year contract worth about 875 million dollars.
reserve.verbatim_source: "a 12 year, $875 Million software and AI contract"
requires: covers two systems, FMDS and SMART

reserve.spoken: Duffy also said this is all the old legacy equipment.
reserve.verbatim_source: "This is all the old legacy equipment."

reserve.verbatim_source: "Our switches, our routers, actually got overloaded with data"

reserve.verbatim_source: "The issue was isolated to two contractor owned and maintained routers that were being updated mid-day."
requires: say PER PASS, an interested party

reserve.spoken: Peyton called it a decision making aid, not a tool that will run rogue.

reserve.verbatim_source: "which is a decision-making aid, and not a tool that's going to run rogue and make weird decisions for the dispatcher," Peyton said.

reserve.spoken: Alaska says Flyways found a better option for 55 percent of its flights.

reserve.verbatim_source: "On average Flyways AI has presented optimization opportunities for 55 percent of Alaska's flights"

The order came out at 11:54 in the morning Alaska time.
